Mathematics and statistics Mathematical matter and equations Italics should be used for mathematical variables and certain physical constants, roman type for operators (such as +, =, d and multipli-cation and integral signs), abbreviations (such as log, sin and exp) and representations of pure numbers (such as e and i). Badly written or ambiguous symbols and signs should be identified for the typesetter (e.g. italic letter “x”/Greek chi/multiplication sign; capital letter “O”/Greek theta/zero), and the spatial relationship of terms made clear. When several brackets have to be used in a math-ematical expression, the sequence should be {[ (...) ] }.
